title: Short-Sale Statement Set-Aside Disbursement — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction
content:
## Short-sale statement set-aside disbursement — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction

On the payoff case of an Approved Short Sale Payoff requested by the borrower of record, the short-sale statement set-aside disbursement that enters the short-sale statement balance is figured from the set-aside, held under the Set-Aside Accounts product, that pays the loan's property charges and from the bills received on it.

| Property-charge set-aside on the loan (Set-Aside Accounts) | Short-sale statement set-aside disbursement |
|---|---|
| an active Fully Funded LESA (Mandatory) or Fully Funded LESA (Borrower-Elected) | the sum of that set-aside's short-sale statement bills, limited to its set-aside balance |
| an active Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve | the sum of that reserve's short-sale statement bills in full, because the reserve's shortfall source pays any part above its balance at once as a corporate advance |
| neither | nothing (0.00) |

**Short-sale statement bills.** A short-sale statement bill is, for each of the three bill types (property tax bill, hazard insurance bill and flood insurance bill), the received bill of that type on the set-aside with the latest due date, when its payment date falls no later than the good-through date, which is 30 calendar days after the statement date. A bill's payment date is its due date less the set-aside plan's tax payment lead days for a tax bill, and less its insurance payment lead days for a hazard or flood bill. A type with no received bill adds nothing, and only the bill carrying the latest due date of each type is looked at. Where several received bills of one type share that latest due date, their billed amounts are taken together as that type's bill.

### Worked case

Hypothetical inputs: a Fully Funded LESA with a set-aside balance of USD 1500.00 and tax and insurance lead days of 15 and 30; a received tax bill of USD 2000.00 whose payment date falls 25 days after the statement date; a received hazard bill of USD 900.00 whose payment date falls 60 days after it; no flood bill. Only the tax bill is a short-sale statement bill (25 days is within the horizon, 60 days is not), so the sum is USD 2000.00 and the short-sale statement set-aside disbursement is that sum limited to the balance, USD 1500.00. Had the same bills sat on an active Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, the short-sale statement set-aside disbursement would be USD 2000.00 in full. All figures are invented for the illustration.
